name: 부대찌개 (Budae Jjigae) · Korean Army Base Stew
description: The postwar stew born from US army rations: Spam, hot dogs, kimchi, tofu and baked beans arranged in a shallow pot with a spicy gochugaru sauce, boiled at the table and finished with instant ramen and American cheese. Serves 4.

ingredients.text: 1 L anchovy-kelp stock, beef stock or chicken stock
ingredients.item: anchovy-kelp stock, beef stock or chicken stock

ingredients.text: 170 g Spam (1/2 can), sliced 5 mm thick
2 hot dogs, sliced on the diagonal
ingredients.item: hot dogs, sliced on the diagonal

ingredients.text: 200 g firm tofu, sliced 1 cm thick
100 g sliced rice cakes (tteok), soaked if hard
ingredients.item: sliced rice cakes (tteok), soaked if hard

ingredients.text: 1 pack instant ramen noodles (discard the seasoning or use half)
ingredients.item: pack instant ramen noodles (discard the seasoning or use half)

steps.text: Mix 2 tbsp gochugaru (Korean chili flakes), 1 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp mirin, 1 tbsp minced garlic, 1 tsp sugar and 1/4 tsp black pepper into a paste.

In a wide shallow pot, arrange 200 g well-fermented kimchi, chopped, 170 g Spam (1/2 can), sliced 5 mm thick, 2 hot dogs, sliced on the diagonal, 200 g firm tofu, sliced 1 cm thick, 1/2 onion, sliced, 100 g enoki or shiitake mushrooms and 100 g sliced rice cakes (tteok), soaked if hard in neat sections around the edge. Spoon 3 tbsp canned baked beans and the sauce into the center and lay 3 scallions, cut into 5 cm lengths on top.
Pour in 1 L anchovy-kelp stock, beef stock or chicken stock around the edge, bring to a boil over high heat and boil 8 minutes, gently stirring the sauce into the broth.

Add 1 pack instant ramen noodles (discard the seasoning or use half) and cook 3 minutes, until the noodles loosen and are just tender. Lay 1 slice American cheese on top and let it melt into the broth.
Serve straight from the pot at the table, ladling into bowls with rice on the side.

notes:
Anchovy-kelp stock is traditional (soak 6 dried anchovies and a 10 cm piece of kombu in 1.2 L water, boil 15 minutes, strain), but beef bone broth (sagol) is what many restaurants use. Spam and kimchi are salty, so taste before adding any salt.

A portable burner at the table is the proper way to eat it: keep it bubbling and add more stock, noodles or rice cakes as it goes.
